BM1-IT202-001 · Course-CLO

verified-syllabus · IT 202 · Computer Programming 1 · academic-semantic

Source

Course: IT 202 - Computer Programming 1
Program: BSIT
Description: This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It
aims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the
development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore
significant real-world applications. 
In line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the
course integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth
but also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute
positively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary
and Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both
technical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith.

Target

Define and analyze the computing requirements needed for an effective solution that is essential for developing holistic and impactful solutions.

BM1-IT202-010 · Course-CLO

verified-syllabus · IT 202 · Computer Programming 1 · academic-semantic

Source

Course: IT 202 - Computer Programming 1
Program: BSIT
Description: This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It
aims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the
development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore
significant real-world applications. 
In line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the
course integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth
but also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute
positively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary
and Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both
technical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith.

Target

 Incorporate ethical standards and social responsibility into technical designs, ensuring that solutions serve the common good, in line with Marian and Augustinian principles of truth and compassion. 

BM1-IT202-019 · Course-CLO

verified-syllabus · IT 202 · Computer Programming 1 · academic-semantic

Source

Course: IT 202 - Computer Programming 1
Program: BSIT
Description: This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It
aims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the
development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore
significant real-world applications. 
In line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the
course integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth
but also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute
positively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary
and Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both
technical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith.

Target

Collaborate effectively within multi-disciplinary and culturally diverse teams to develop Java- based programming solutions that address social challenges, demonstrating social responsibility and cultural sensitivity.

BM1-IT202-031 · Course-CLO

verified-syllabus · IT 202 · Computer Programming 1 · academic-semantic

Source

Course: IT 202 - Computer Programming 1
Program: BSIT
Description: This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It
aims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the
development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore
significant real-world applications. 
In line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the
course integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth
but also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute
positively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary
and Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both
technical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith.

Target

Demonstrate the Filipino- Catholic Augustinian Spirituality through value webbing.

  "description": [
    {
      "id": "it202_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It\naims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the\ndevelopment of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore\nsignificant real-world applications. \nIn line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the\ncourse integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth\nbut also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute\npositively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary\nand Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both\ntechnical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith."

Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore\nsignificant real-world applications. \nIn line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the\ncourse integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth\nbut also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute\npositively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary\nand Saint Augustine. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore\nsignificant real-world applications. \nIn line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the\ncourse integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth\nbut also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. BM1-IT202-062 · ILO-CLO

verified-syllabus · IT 202 · Computer Programming 1 · academic-semantic

Source

Define and analyze the computing requirements needed for an effective solution that is essential for developing holistic and impactful solutions.

Target

ILO1: Utilize various looping constructs (for, while, do-while) in Java to execute repeated tasks, and design programs that efficiently handle repetitive processes and iterations, incorporating loops to solve real-world problems. CLO1 CLO2, CLO3

    {
      "id": "it202_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It\naims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the\ndevelopment of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore\nsignificant real-world applications. \nIn line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the\ncourse integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth\nbut also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute\npositively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary\nand Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both\ntechnical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith."
    }

This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute\npositively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary\nand Saint Augustine.   "description": [
    {
      "id": "it202_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It\naims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the\ndevelopment of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore\nsignificant real-world applications. \nIn line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the\ncourse integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth\nbut also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute\npositively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary\nand Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both\ntechnical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith."
    }

This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute\npositively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary\nand Saint Augustine.     {
      "id": "it202_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It\naims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the\ndevelopment of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore\nsignificant real-world applications. \nIn line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the\ncourse integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth\nbut also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute\npositively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary\nand Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both\ntechnical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith."
    }

Target

This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It
aims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the
development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore
significant real-world applications. 
In line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the
course integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth
but also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute
positively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary
and Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both
technical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith.

BM1-IT202-126 · CLO-classification

verified-syllabus · IT 202 · Computer Programming 1 · academic-semantic

Source

Computer Programming 1
BSIT
This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It
aims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the
development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore
significant real-world applications. 
In line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the
course integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth
but also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute
positively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary
and Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both
technical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith.
Assigned classification: Introductory

Target

Define and analyze the computing requirements needed for an effective solution that is essential for developing holistic and impactful solutions.

development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore
significant real-world applications. 
In line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the
course integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth
but also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute
positively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary
and Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both
technical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith.
Assigned classification: Introductory

Target

Collaborate effectively within multi-disciplinary and culturally diverse teams to develop Java- based programming solutions that address social challenges, demonstrating social responsibility and cultural sensitivity.

This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute\npositively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary\nand Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both\ntechnical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith."
    }

Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore\nsignificant real-world applications. \nIn line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the\ncourse integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth\nbut also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute\npositively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary\nand Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both\ntechnical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith."
    }
  ],

This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute\npositively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary\nand Saint Augustine.     {
      "id": "it202_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It\naims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the\ndevelopment of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore\nsignificant real-world applications. \nIn line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the\ncourse integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth\nbut also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute\npositively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary\nand Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both\ntechnical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith."
    }

Statements
• Java Loops
▪ For Loops
▪ Do While Loop
▪ Break/Continue

- ILO2. Inference the structured programming concepts aCLOng with the Java syntax to implement them.

Source

Week 1 course content: I. Orientation
A. Introduction to the
Course Contents
B. Course
Requirements and
Activities
C. Course Objectives
Grading System and
Policies on Absences,
Tardiness and
Examinations
ILOs:
- ILO 1: Demonstrate a clear understanding of the course structure, expectations, and key programming concepts in Java, including how these skills align with real- world IT challenges and professional ethical standards. [CLO1]
Learning activities: • Setting and sharing of Expectations from the Course • Discussion on the Vision, Mission and Goals of LCUP and of CITE • Presentation of Course Objectives and Contents, Course Requirements and Activities Review of Policies on Absences, Tardiness, Examinations, Grading System
Assessment tasks: • Statement of Expectations • Review of Course Contents, Objectives, Activities and Assessment Tools • Review of Policies on Absences, Tardiness, Examinations, Grading System
Definitions of the values named (from the institution's published wording; approval status: pending_approval):
- Compassion: Compassion is love in action. It means going beyond sympathy and extending genuine care by understanding the feelings of others, recognizing their needs, and responding with kindness. Through compassion, we reflect God’s love by becoming instruments of comfort and support to those who are most in need.
- Courage: Courage is the strength to stand firm in truth and goodness. It is the freedom to express one’s thoughts responsibly, the boldness to give and receive fraternal correction, and the integrity to choose what is right even when it is difficult or unpopular. Rooted in Gospel values, courage empowers us to live authentically and faithfully in service of God and others.

Target

• Compassion
• Courage
• Open
mindedness
• Respect
• Obedience

Definitions of the values named (from the institution's published wording; approval status: pending_approval):
- Courage: Courage is the strength to stand firm in truth and goodness. It is the freedom to express one’s thoughts responsibly, the boldness to give and receive fraternal correction, and the integrity to choose what is right even when it is difficult or unpopular. Rooted in Gospel values, courage empowers us to live authentically and faithfully in service of God and others.
- Interiority: Interiority is the practice of turning inward, encountering our true selves, and allowing God’s presence to transform us. Through prayer, reflection, and contemplative silence, we confront our weaknesses and sinfulness, but also rediscover our dignity as children of God. This journey within leads us to an authentic relationship with Him and guides us to live with clarity and peace.

Language
ILOs:
- ILO3: Understand the fundamentals of structured logic using decisions, loops, and array manipulation. [CLO 1] [CLO3]
- ILO4: Be able to apply conditional statements in Java to control program flow based on specific conditions, and write programs that make decisions dynamically depending on user input or computed values. [CLO 2] [CLO3]
Learning activities: • Discussion using PowerPoint Presentation • Video Presentation • Laboratory Exercises: Machine Language Group Dynamics

Definitions of the values named (from the institution's published wording; approval status: pending_approval):
- Courage: Courage is the strength to stand firm in truth and goodness. It is the freedom to express one’s thoughts responsibly, the boldness to give and receive fraternal correction, and the integrity to choose what is right even when it is difficult or unpopular. Rooted in Gospel values, courage empowers us to live authentically and faithfully in service of God and others.
- Humility: Humility allows us to see ourselves and others through the lens of truth and grace. It teaches us to acknowledge both our strengths and limitations, to welcome correction with openness, and to use every experience as an opportunity for growth. Above all, humility reminds us to be grateful to God who created each of us uniquely for a purpose greater than ourselves.

Source

Week 9-11 course content: XI. Looping
Statements
• Java Loops
▪ For Loops
▪ Do While Loop
▪ Break/Continue
ILOs:
- ILO1: Utilize various looping constructs (for, while, do-while) in Java to execute repeated tasks, and design programs that efficiently handle repetitive processes and iterations, incorporating loops to solve real-world problems. CLO1 CLO2, CLO3
- ILO2. Inference the structured programming concepts aCLOng with the Java syntax to implement them.
Learning activities: • Discussion using PowerPoint Presentation • Functioning Knowledge • Laboratory Exercises.
Assessment tasks: • Recitation • Group Participation • Quiz • Machine Problem
Definitions of the values named (from the institution's published wording; approval status: pending_approval):
- Humility: Humility allows us to see ourselves and others through the lens of truth and grace. It teaches us to acknowledge both our strengths and limitations, to welcome correction with openness, and to use every experience as an opportunity for growth. Above all, humility reminds us to be grateful to God who created each of us uniquely for a purpose greater than ourselves.

Target

• Critical
Thinking
• Understanding
• Precision
• Accuracy
• Appreciation
• Humility

Week 14 course content: XIII. Strings
• String Manipulation
➢ Length()
➢ charAt()
➢ indexOf()
➢ concat()
➢ replace
➢ ignorecase()
➢ substring()
ILOs:
- ILO1: Apply various string manipulation methods in Java. [CLO 1-2] .
- LO2: Synthesize skills in De-bugging Java Language program. [CLO2-3]
Learning activities: Lecture: • Discussion using Powerpoint Presentation • Quiz • Laboratory: :Exercises: ➢ Machine Problem • Seatwork using trial and error discovery learning
Assessment tasks: • Recitation • Quiz • Seatwork-Trial and Error for discovery learning • Accurate Program output
Definitions of the values named (from the institution's published wording; approval status: pending_approval):
- Courage: Courage is the strength to stand firm in truth and goodness. It is the freedom to express one’s thoughts responsibly, the boldness to give and receive fraternal correction, and the integrity to choose what is right even when it is difficult or unpopular. Rooted in Gospel values, courage empowers us to live authentically and faithfully in service of God and others.
- Humility: Humility allows us to see ourselves and others through the lens of truth and grace. It teaches us to acknowledge both our strengths and limitations, to welcome correction with openness, and to use every experience as an opportunity for growth. Above all, humility reminds us to be grateful to God who created each of us uniquely for a purpose greater than ourselves.

Target

• Critical
Thinking
• Active
participation
and
involvement
• Open
mindedness
• Humility
• Patience
• Courage

Assessment tasks: • Recitation • Quiz • Machine problem: Hands-on exercises using C programs
Definitions of the values named (from the institution's published wording; approval status: pending_approval):
- Courage: Courage is the strength to stand firm in truth and goodness. It is the freedom to express one’s thoughts responsibly, the boldness to give and receive fraternal correction, and the integrity to choose what is right even when it is difficult or unpopular. Rooted in Gospel values, courage empowers us to live authentically and faithfully in service of God and others.
- Interiority: Interiority is the practice of turning inward, encountering our true selves, and allowing God’s presence to transform us. Through prayer, reflection, and contemplative silence, we confront our weaknesses and sinfulness, but also rediscover our dignity as children of God. This journey within leads us to an authentic relationship with Him and guides us to live with clarity and peace.

BM1-IT202-180 · Title-description

verified-syllabus · IT 202 · Computer Programming 1 · academic-semantic

Source

Course title: Computer Programming 1
Course code: IT 202
Program: BSIT

Target

This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It
aims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the
development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore
significant real-world applications. 
In line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the
course integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth
but also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute
positively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary
and Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both
technical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith.

Source

Course title: Computer Programming 1
Course code: IT 202
Program: BSIT
Course objectives (CLOs):
CLO 1: Define and analyze the computing requirements needed for an effective solution that is essential for developing holistic and impactful solutions.
CLO 2:  Incorporate ethical standards and social responsibility into technical designs, ensuring that solutions serve the common good, in line with Marian and Augustinian principles of truth and compassion. 
CLO 3: Collaborate effectively within multi-disciplinary and culturally diverse teams to develop Java- based programming solutions that address social challenges, demonstrating social responsibility and cultural sensitivity.
CLO 4: Demonstrate the Filipino- Catholic Augustinian Spirituality through value webbing.

Source

Week 9-11 course content: XI. Looping
Statements
• Java Loops
▪ For Loops
▪ Do While Loop
▪ Break/Continue
ILOs:
- ILO1: Utilize various looping constructs (for, while, do-while) in Java to execute repeated tasks, and design programs that efficiently handle repetitive processes and iterations, incorporating loops to solve real-world problems. CLO1 CLO2, CLO3
- ILO2. Inference the structured programming concepts aCLOng with the Java syntax to implement them.
Course-wide contact units (not lesson requirements or proof of resource availability): lecture 2, laboratory 1
Learning activities: • Discussion using PowerPoint Presentation • Functioning Knowledge • Laboratory Exercises.

Target

•
Recitation
• Group Participation
• Quiz
• Machine Problem

{
  "meta": {
    "program": "BSIT",
    "code": "IT 202",
    "title": "Computer Programming 1",
    "schoolYear": "2025-2026",
    "curriculumYear": "",
    "yearLevel": "",
    "prereq": "IT 101",
    "lecture": "2",
    "lab": "1"
  },
  "description": [
    {
      "id": "it202_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It\naims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the\ndevelopment of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore\nsignificant real-world applications. \nIn line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the\ncourse integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth\nbut also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute\npositively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary\nand Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both\ntechnical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith."
    }
  ],

  "description": [
    {
      "id": "it202_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It\naims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the\ndevelopment of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore\nsignificant real-world applications. \nIn line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the\ncourse integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth\nbut also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute\npositively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary\nand Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both\ntechnical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith."
    }

      "id": "it202_desc",
      "t": "This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It\naims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the\ndevelopment of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore\nsignificant real-world applications. \nIn line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the\ncourse integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth\nbut also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute\npositively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary\nand Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both\ntechnical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith."
    }

Rooted in Gospel values, courage empowers us to live authentically and faithfully in service of God and others.

Target

Courage: explain a decision and revise it after evidence-based peer feedback.

BM1-S01-032 · Week1-introduction

synthetic · IT 202 · COMPUTER PROGRAMMING 1 (FUNDAMENTALS OF PROGRAMMING) · academic-semantic

Source

Course title: COMPUTER PROGRAMMING 1 (FUNDAMENTALS OF PROGRAMMING)
Course code: IT 202
Program: BSIT
Course objectives (CLOs):
CLO 1: Explain the concepts of Java conditional statements and input validation.
CLO 2: Implement and test Java if/else statements for the stated input-validation rules.
CLO 3: Demonstrate and justify a solution involving Java conditional statements and input validation.
CLO 4: Practice honest reporting and responsible teamwork while studying Java conditional statements and input validation.

Target

Introduction to COMPUTER PROGRAMMING 1 (FUNDAMENTALS OF PROGRAMMING) and the supplied course objectives
Explain the course subject and the supplied course objectives.
Trace worked examples, then write and test Java conditional programs in pairs with annotated instructions.
